NIT Trichy & Surathkal Research Map

DPCN A2 · Team 12

NIT Trichy vs NIT Surathkal: research 2016–2026

Every paper by regular science and engineering faculty of both NITs, from OpenAlex, with their citation and co-authorship networks. Citation counts as of ; field-weighted impact (FWCI) as of . Instructor: Chittaranjan Hens.

AI & research trends

Is AI spreading into every department, and how recent is the work each department builds on? (Team insight analyses, scripts/insights.py.) These charts cover both NITs together.

AI papers as a share of all papers

A paper counts as AI if its OpenAlex subfield is an AI field or its title names an AI method. Computing = CSE, IT, Computer Applications.

Outside computing, AI arrives as a tool, not a topic

AI papers outside computing departments, by the method named in the title.

AI share by department

2016–2018 vs 2023–2025.

Are AI papers cited more?

Median FWCI of AI vs other papers in the same department (departments with 20+ AI papers).

AI share by department and year

Share of each department's papers that are AI (%). Darker = more AI; gray numbers = fewer than 10 papers that year. 2026 is a partial year.

How recent are the references? (Price index)

Share of references at most 4 years older than the citing paper. Higher = closer to the research front.

Recent references, higher impact

Median FWCI of papers grouped into fifths by their Price index.

Price index by department

2016–2018 vs 2023–2025: every department is moving towards newer work.

Co-authorship network

Faculty are nodes; a link means at least one joint paper. Degree = number of faculty co-authors, betweenness = how often a person sits on the shortest path between others, communities from Louvain.

Degree distribution

Rich club

ρ(k) > 1: faculty with more than k co-authors link to each other more than in random graphs with the same degrees.

Communities found (Louvain)

Who works with whom? (assortativity)

How the network grew

The faculty co-authorship network year by year (cumulative from 2016), how new links form, and whether we can predict them. (Team insight analyses, scripts/insights.py.)

Faculty and links

Connected faculty (at least one faculty co-author) and links, cumulative.

Densification

Links against faculty, log–log, one point per year. A slope above 1 means links grow faster than people.

A giant component forms

Share of faculty in the largest connected group.

The network shrinks in distance

Effective diameter (90% of pairs within this many steps).

Departments slowly mix

Louvain modularity and the share of cross-department links.

Do friends of friends become co-authors?

How much more likely a pair is to start working together next year than a far-apart pair (triadic closure).

Where new links come from

New faculty–faculty links each year, by how they formed.

Closure inside and across groups

Chance (%) that a pair starts collaborating the next year.

Predicting new collaborations

Precision of the top-k predictions

Share of the k highest-scored pairs that really started collaborating in 2023–2026.

What the learned model relies on

Standardised logistic-regression coefficients.

Most likely future collaborations (top 50)

Faculty pairs with no joint paper yet, ranked by the learned model.

Indian connections

How each NIT links to other Indian institutes. A citation between two papers that share an institute through co-authorship is not counted as a link (e.g. NIT Trichy citing its own paper with IIT Madras).

Citation flow with other Indian institutes

Citations received from and given to other Indian institutes, by year of the citing paper. Solid = received, dashed = given.

Impact ratio

Citations received ÷ citations made, by publication year. Recent papers have had little time to be cited, so the ratio falls towards 2026.

Co-authored papers by type of partner

A paper counts once for each partner on it (log scale). All non-NIT clusters are cross-cluster links.

Strongest co-authorship partners

Top 10 per NIT by shared papers. Joint-paper FWCI = mean field-weighted impact of the papers written with that partner; the chip shows the gap to the NIT's own average (does collaborating pay off?).

Top 10 Indian institutes citing us

Citations from the partner's papers to ours (the other NIT left out).

Partners worth approaching

Similar research topics (Jaccard of subfields) and heavy citation exchange, but at most 5 joint papers.

Hub faculty

Faculty who connect their NIT with the most other Indian institutes.

The knowledge hierarchy

Where our partners are

Indian institutes linked to the NIT (co-authorship or 30+ citations exchanged). Bubble size = joint papers; gray = citations only. Stars = our NITs.

Gravity model

Poisson regression on partner size and distance. Elasticity = % change for a 1% longer distance.

People work locally, knowledge travels

Both NITs together: the share of all joint papers and of all citations exchanged with Indian partners, by distance from the NIT.

Topic similarity vs joint papers

Each dot is a main partner: weighted Jaccard similarity of research subfields against shared papers (log).

Most-cited papers that cite us

Top papers from other Indian institutes that cite each NIT (retracted papers left out).

Who's better?

Raw counts favour different NITs on different measures. Here the two are compared fairly: field-weighted impact, branch by branch, with statistical tests.

Measures from class

IF = the journal's 2-year mean citedness (OpenAlex), the impact-factor formula on open data.

Is one institute better overall?

Regression of log(1 + FWCI) per paper on an NIT Surathkal indicator, adding controls.

Which NIT is stronger in each branch?

Mean FWCI per branch, NIT Trichy minus NIT Surathkal, with a 95% bootstrap interval. Gray: no clear difference.

Branch comparison

Branches with at least 8 publishing faculty. Click a column to sort.

Network science

Per faculty member (Mann–Whitney test)

Medians per faculty member with papers, and whether the gap is significant at 5%.

Is there a large-paper bias?

Rankings and network with different caps on the number of authors per paper.

Branch head to head

Branches both NITs have. Blue = NIT Trichy higher, orange = NIT Surathkal higher.

Class measures per branch

Publications, Q1 papers and papers in IF > 5 / IF > 10 journals, per branch.

How we built it

From the institutes' own faculty pages to the networks: every number on this dashboard comes from the scripts in our repository and can be re-run.

The pipeline

Rules we applied

    Sources

    Faculty roster

    Regular faculty from the institutes' pages, 2016–2026 (one archived copy per year).

    Limitations

      Phase II additions

      The professor's Phase II suggestions (scripts/phase2.py). Publication statistics now also count papers by students and other NIT staff (an NIT author but no faculty author); the networks and faculty rankings stay faculty-only. Panels follow the institute switch.

      Papers per year: faculty papers vs all papers

      All papers = faculty papers + papers with an NIT author but no NIT faculty author. 2026 is a partial year.

      Students' own papers are not weaker

      Papers with an NIT author but no NIT faculty author (mostly research scholars).

      Publication statistics in both scopes

      Q1 and IF together: a paper counts only if its journal is Q1 and has IF above the threshold (IF = OpenAlex 2-year mean citedness).

      Papers by number of authors

      Fewer than 10 authors vs 10 or more.

      Large teams and very high citations

      The checks for physics-style large collaborations and 1-lakh-citation profiles.

      Q1 papers in journals with IF > 5 and IF > 10, by department

      Faculty papers. Sorted by Q1 and IF > 5.

      Collaborating institutions per year

      Distinct other institutions on each year's papers (all papers). The other NIT counts as a partner. 2026 is partial.

      Why do private universities cite us so much?

      The 40 institutes that cite our faculty papers most (18 private, 22 public). Medians per institute, Mann–Whitney test.

      Top 30 publications by journal impact factor

      Ordered by the journal's IF, ties by the paper's citations. SCImago-ranked journals only. Both NITs.

      Each faculty member's top 10 papers by journal IF

      Most-used journals and conferences

      Top 25 journals and top 15 conference venues. Repository deposits (Zenodo, DOAJ) are left out.

      Research score vs collaboration score

      Four profiles

      Split at the median of each score (current faculty with 10+ papers).

      Collaboration ranking

      Collaboration score = mean percentile of NIT faculty co-authors, Indian partner institutes and foreign partner institutes. The research score (7 measures) is unchanged.

      Institute-level co-authorship network

      Indian institutes on our papers (students' papers included), linked when they appear on the same paper. Both NITs.

      Most important partner institutes (betweenness)

      By institute type

      Research questions

      Thirteen questions answered with our data (scripts/questions.py, details in data/analysis/questions/QUESTIONS.md). "Adjusted" = compared with papers of the same field and year, venue type, team size and NIT (regression on log(1 + FWCI), robust errors). Bars show 95% confidence intervals; gray = not significant.

        15 · Which countries do we work with, and does it help?

        Top 15 partner countries

        2026 is partial.

        16 · Does partnering with stronger institutes raise impact?

        Impact difference by partner type

        Adjusted FWCI difference when this partner type is on the paper.

        Partner types

        Papers (both NITs), raw mean FWCI and adjusted difference.

        17 · Key-person risk: what if hub faculty leave?

        How the faculty network breaks

        Pairs of faculty who can still reach each other as faculty are removed: bridges first (betweenness, recomputed), most-connected first, or at random (mean of 100 runs).

        Most critical people overall

        Share of all connected faculty pairs cut if this one person leaves.

        Who holds each department together?

        Inside each department's own collaboration network: the person whose departure cuts most pairs.

        25 · "Rich get richer": do well-cited papers gain citations faster?

        Attachment kernel

        New citations next year (relative to papers of the same year and age) against citations already received (log–log). A slope of 1 is linear preferential attachment.

        Early winners stay winners

        Papers in the top 10% after 2 years that are still in the top 10% after 5 years, by publication year.

        26 · How much do departments cite their own institute?

        Citations received from home, by department

        Self = the citing paper shares an author with the cited one; colleague = another person from the same NIT. Indian citing papers only, so these are lower bounds.

        Home share by publication year

        Solid = citations received from home; dashed = references pointing home. 2016–2025 (2026 is partial and its early citations are mostly self-citations).

        Departments

        Faculty papers; departments with 50+ papers. Rank = rank by citations per paper among the 28 departments.

        Outside papers citing 10+ of ours, by year

        Papers with no author from our NITs.

        The 40 institutes that cite us most

        Share of each institute's citations to us that come from heavy citing papers (10+ of ours), from its single biggest author, and going to our single most-cited faculty member. ★ = that author published with an NIT affiliation earlier.

        The heaviest outside citing papers

        Outside papers that cite the most of our papers. A statistical signal for follow-up, not a judgement about anyone: citing relevant earlier work of your group is normal.
